root_cause.text: The zynqmp_nvmem efuse access function used the size of the length variable (`sizeof(bytes)`) and caller-controlled `bytes` in `memcpy` instead of the actual destination object sizes, causing an undersized DMA buffer allocation and over-copy into the local `value` variable.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `dma_alloc_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), ...)` and matching `dma_free_coherent(..., sizeof(bytes), ...)` to use `bytes`, and changes `memcpy(&value, val, bytes)` to `memcpy(&value, val, sizeof(value))`; the commit message explicitly states the wrong buffer size in DMA allocation and memcpy could cause undersized DMA buffer access and memory corruption.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use an unsigned temporary for eFuse word values to prevent incorrect sign-based handling of the data.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration in zynqmp_efuse_access() was changed from "int value;" to "unsigned int value;" with no other code modifications shown.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this changes the signedness of the temporary value used in the function so it is treated as a non-negative 32-bit quantity, avoiding sign-related interpretation issues when handling eFuse word data.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix zynqmp efuse write validation by copying the full value-sized input before checking PUF-related bit masks.
intent_record.what: The memcpy call in zynqmp_efuse_access() was changed from copying 'bytes' bytes from 'val' into the local variable 'value' to always copying sizeof(value) bytes instead.
intent_record.how: This ensures the local 'value' variable is fully populated before its bitmask checks are performed, preventing partial copies based on the caller-provided byte count from causing incorrect validation or use of uninitialized portions of 'value' during EFUSE write handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix zynqmp_efuse_access() to allocate a DMA buffer using the requested byte count rather than the size of the length variable.
intent_record.what: The size argument passed to dma_alloc_coherent() was changed from sizeof(bytes) to bytes in zynqmp_efuse_access().
intent_record.how: This makes the DMA buffer allocation use the runtime byte count requested instead of the size of the bytes variable itself, preventing under-allocation and ensuring the buffer is large enough for the intended efuse data transfer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix dma_free_coherent() to free the efuse data buffer with the correct allocation size.
intent_record.what: The size argument in the dma_free_coherent() call for freeing the data buffer was changed from sizeof(bytes) to bytes.
intent_record.how: This makes the coherent DMA buffer be freed using the actual allocated buffer length instead of the size of the bytes variable itself, preventing incorrect DMA memory deallocation behavior when cleaning up after efuse access.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix zynqmp eFuse write validation and data handling by correctly reading the full input word and using an appropriate unsigned type for bitmask-based checks.
Correct the DMA buffer allocation and deallocation sizes in zynqmp_efuse_access() so the efuse data buffer is managed using the actual requested byte count.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly modify zynqmp eFuse data copying/validation to use the full value-sized input instead of an incorrect length, which is tied to the root cause of using the wrong size in memcpy and mishandling copied eFuse data.

The changes directly fix the root cause by replacing use of sizeof(bytes) with the actual requested byte count for DMA allocation/free in zynqmp_efuse_access(), addressing the undersized buffer issue that led to unsafe copying.

candidates.rationale: Allocates the DMA buffer using the size of the length variable rather than the requested byte count, directly causing an undersized buffer.
Copies a caller-controlled number of bytes into local variable value instead of limiting the copy to the size of the destination object, enabling overwrite of the local variable.
Uses the wrong size when freeing the DMA buffer, reflecting the same incorrect size assumption as the allocation and indicating the vulnerable buffer management logic.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation uses sizeof(bytes) instead of the actual requested byte count, producing an undersized DMA buffer. That directly matches the root cause of allocating based on the size of the length variable rather than the destination/data size.

This memcpy uses caller-controlled bytes as the copy length into local variable value, without bounding it to the size of value. That matches the root cause of over-copy into the local value variable.
This free mirrors the same incorrect sizeof(bytes) assumption as the allocation site, confirming the vulnerable buffer size logic around the DMA buffer lifecycle.

Author: Praveen Teja Kundanala <praveen.teja.kundanala@amd.com>

    nvmem: zynqmp_nvmem: Add support to access efuse
    
    Add support to read/write efuse memory map of ZynqMP.
    Below are the offsets of ZynqMP efuse memory map
            0 - SOC version(read only)
            0xC - 0xFC -ZynqMP specific purpose efuses
            0x100 - 0x17F - Physical Unclonable Function(PUF)
                    efu
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is fully visible in `zynqmp_efuse_access()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The root cause is present in two places. First, the DMA buffer is allocated with `data = dma_alloc_coherent(dev, sizeof(bytes), &dma_buf, GFP_KERNEL);`, which allocates only `sizeof(bytes)` bytes (the size of the `size_t` variable), not the caller-requested payload size. Second, the function then copies `bytes` bytes into and out of that buffer with `memcpy(data, val, bytes);` for writes and `memcpy(val, data, bytes);` for reads. This creates the exact undersized-allocation/over-copy condition described in the root cause. Additionally, in the PUF write path it does `memcpy(&value, val, bytes);` where `value` is an `int`, so a caller-controlled `bytes` can exceed the destination object size and overflow the local variable. Because these incorrect size uses are present and there is no bounding such as allocating `bytes` for `data` or limiting the copy into `value` to `sizeof(value)`, the function contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.

This uses `sizeof(bytes)` (the size of the `size_t` variable, typically 8) instead of the requested payload length `bytes`, which can under-allocate the DMA buffer.
